task: Literature and experimental-protocol support for Wikipedia cold start of VeRA and a foundation vector bank

scope.retrieval: First attempted the five Hugging Face paper .md pages; the web tool reported all inaccessible. Subsequently read arXiv HTML, the original ACL PDF, and official author repositories. No third-party summaries were used as evidence.

papers.title: Large Memory Layers with Product Keys
papers.corpus: Common Crawl news, 28 billion words / 140GB; not Wikipedia, and words must not be relabeled as tokenizer tokens.
papers.mechanism: Queries retrieve from the product of two trainable sub-key codebooks; top-k weights mix trainable values. Only selected values receive gradients from that input. Heads share values.
papers.initialization_and_gradients: Random keys; query BatchNorm increases coverage; sparse values use a higher Adam learning rate of 1e-3. No dense-backward or semantic clustering/merging scheme.
papers.concrete_evidence: Table 2: query-BN comparison for 1M slots increases usage from 25.8314% to 80.3043% and reduces PPL from 19.7913 to 17.9819.
papers.relevance: Directly supports learning a foundation K/V dictionary on a large corpus and measuring usage. Does not establish an equivalent implementation with one rank64 VeRA layer on frozen Qwen or guarantee individual fact writes/overwrites.

papers.title: Large Product Key Memory for Pretrained Language Models
papers.corpus: English Wikipedia + BookCorpus，17GB；BERTBASE MLM，500,000 steps，batch 1024 sequences。
papers.mechanism: First pretrains without memory, then initializes a memory-augmented model. ResM retains the original FFN and adds a PKM residual rather than replacing the FFN.
papers.initialization_and_gradients: Sparse-value LR 1e-3; other Adam LR 1e-4. Discusses stale slots and backbone drift without switching to dense value gradients.
papers.concrete_evidence: Layer 4 top-32 usage can approach 100% while top-1 is around 2%; initialization + ResM raises top-1 above 95%. Top-k hit coverage alone can therefore hide degeneration.
papers.relevance: The closest match to cold start and sparse-utilization degeneration. Its backbone is jointly trained; generated VDB records with our frozen backbone are a different mechanism. Current failures cannot directly be diagnosed as catastrophic drift.

papers.title: Memory Layers at Scale
papers.corpus: Llama-like pretraining from scratch: up to 1T tokens, base 134M–8B, memory up to 128B parameters. A small Wikipedia fine-tune is not a reproduction.
papers.mechanism: Trainable product-key sparse lookup; Memory+ shares values across layers and adds a SiLU input gate and output projection. qk-normalization addresses instability in large memory layers.
papers.initialization_and_gradients: The paper still uses sparse reads/updates of selected K/V and does not claim gradients for all values. Official implementation initialization is recorded separately in official_code_check.
papers.concrete_evidence: At fixed parameter count, multiple memory layers improve performance up to about 3 layers; replacing more FFNs then degrades it.
papers.relevance: Supports first training a useful shared foundation dictionary and studying multilayer readout/gating. This is not online fact-vector writing and does not establish sufficient single-layer VeRA capacity.

papers.title: SHINE: A Scalable In-Context Hypernetwork for Mapping Context to LoRA in a Single Pass
papers.corpus: TransMLA 6B-token corpus, 1 epoch. Wikitext-2 is only a reconstruction/completion evaluation; pretraining must not be described as Wikipedia 6B.
papers.mechanism: Freezes Qwen3-8B, extracts cross-layer states through Meta LoRA/memory tokens, and generates LoRA with a Transformer. Reconstruction + completion precede QA instruction tuning.
papers.initialization_and_gradients: Pretraining uses full-sequence CE for context-conditioned parameter generation. There is no top-k VDB, hence no solution to sparse-slot coverage.
papers.concrete_evidence: Section 4.1: reconstruction and completion are equally likely. For completion, the writer sees only the first 70–90% of context while the target remains the full text.
papers.relevance: Strongly supports learning the text-to-parameters-to-text interface before QA. Its cross-layer multitoken capacity is much greater than one pooled rank64 value; gains cannot be attributed solely to data scale.

papers.title: Token Merging: Your ViT But Faster
papers.corpus: Visual/video/audio Transformers, including ImageNet; not Wikipedia or language-model parameter memory.
papers.mechanism: Bipartite matching by key similarity; merging weighted by token size; log(size) added to attention to retain duplicate-token weight. Gradients propagate through pooling.
papers.initialization_and_gradients: No Gumbel/ST required. No proof of dense gradients for learnable long-term memory slots or recovery of dead slots.
papers.concrete_evidence: Table 2 compares k-means and matching; the paper does not conclude that clustering automatically improves performance.
papers.relevance: Supports careful differentiable compression and preservation of quality/count information only. It is not evidence that merging entity facts preserves exact overwrites or prevents sparse-gradient degeneration.

official_code_check.section: HashingMemory.reset_parameters lines 211–243; forward/get_indices lines 246–355 (observed main, not immutable commit)
observations: Keys: uniform[-1/sqrt(key_dim),+1/sqrt(key_dim)]; values: Normal(0,value_dim^-0.5); first query layer: Xavier uniform.
Softmax after top-k; values(indices,scores) aggregation; separate value_fixed_lr=0.001 by default. Neither k-means initialization nor dense backward for unselected values.

Query BN is disabled by default, and code warns that padding contaminates statistics. Paper qk-normalization may not exactly match this single repository file. Pin commit/configuration rather than assuming implementation from the paper name.

synthesis.strongest_support: There are direct precedents for first training a stable memory interface/foundation dictionary on Wikipedia or general corpora, then training the task. Here only the module is cold-started; Qwen remains a pretrained backbone.
synthesis.not_established: The literature does not guarantee that more corpus data, greater slot coverage, or clustering solves semantic generalization in editable VeRA memory. It does not establish sparse gradients alone as the cause of current failure.
three_distinct_targets: Foundation codebook: shared K/V parameters trained offline, persistently changed through backpropagation.
Episodic VDB: a writer generates new-document records by forward pass; records are independently editable, with shared parameters frozen at test time.
Writer/reader: connects documents to the key/value parameter interface. Improvements in a general LM codebook do not automatically establish writable new documents.

gradient_design.status: The following are algebraic derivations and proposed diagnostic controls, not a recipe validated by the papers above.
gradient_design.sparse: p_s=softmax(logits[topk]) scattered into N; y_s=p_s @ V. Both forward and backward supply task gradients only to selected value rows; shared generated Wv requires separate interpretation.
gradient_design.routing_only_st: p_ST=p_d+stopgrad(p_s-p_d); y=p_ST@V. Forward is sparse; router gradients come from dense p_d, but dL/dV still multiplies forward p_ST=p_s. It therefore does not give gradients to all values.
gradient_design.output_level_st: y_d=p_d@V; y_ST=y_d+stopgrad(y_s-y_d). Forward equals y_s numerically; backward for K/query/V uses the dense y_d Jacobian and can cover all values.
caveats: Output-level ST is a biased surrogate, not the true gradient of the actual top-k objective.
Tiny dense-softmax weights can underflow or be effectively zero; nonzero coverage is not effective learning.
Dense backward requires O(N*rank) aggregation. Training must not be advertised as sparse; record training and deployment costs separately.

If value=Wv(feature), one shared-Wv gradient affects future generated values for all records. Generated slots must not be treated as independent embedding parameters when interpreting frozen/update coverage.
Adam momentum/weight decay can change rows without current-step gradients. Record gradient norm, parameter delta, and actual read weight separately; they are not interchangeable.

proposed_minimal_design.status: Recommendations for the coordinating agent to decide on implementation. This review fixed no execution budget and started no jobs.
data: Split a fixed Wikipedia snapshot by article_id/title/page hash before chunking, clustering, or constructing the foundation dictionary; hold out near-duplicates.
Record actual unique articles, unique tokens, and token exposures. A WikiText subset is not all of Wikipedia or equivalent to 6B-token pretraining.
initialization: Initialize new VeRA/writer/codebook from scratch without loading the old 16-word synthetic-task adapter. Keep frozen Qwen and the original FFN, adding a residual branch.

First verify that cold initialization preserves base NLL/outputs and yields finite, effective K/V/router gradients. Zeroing gate/output matrix/values together blocks gradients; zero only one point at a time and record first-step paths.
Compare uniform-random keys with k-means++ keys in training-token query space at equal N/rank. A raw support-feature centroid must not be presented as an already aligned query key.
routing_controls: R0: ordinary top-k forward/backward as the actual sparse baseline.
R1: dense-softmax early training, annealed to the same top-k on a fixed schedule; final inference is sparse only. Improvement over R0 establishes an optimization-schedule effect only.
R2: output-level ST with sparse forward and dense surrogate backward throughout. Match data/token exposures and separately account for extra computation.
Fix initialization when comparing R0/R1/R2, then add clustering to the smallest credible design. Do not simultaneously change writer, basis, layer count, and loss and lose attribution.
memory_merge_controls: Begin with train-only centroid initialization and learning at fixed N, without online fact merging, to isolate optimization effects.
If merging is additionally tested, retain slot mass and original-member mappings. Consider log-mass weight correction for identical-key merges and check whether top-k ordering changes.
Merging different entities/relations with similar hidden states can lose distinctions. Similar keys do not guarantee functionally equivalent values; require task-loss or behavioral checks.

Actual merging changes total capacity, parameter count, and softmax mass. Compare with random/uniform compression to the same final slot count and an unmerged baseline. A smaller usage denominator is not an improvement.
Foundation codebooks can be clustered. Initially avoid irreversible merging of independently overwritable episodic facts, or retain original records for reconstruction.
objectives: Foundation-dictionary stage: causal Wikipedia next-token CE can use only prefix-visible information; evaluate held-out NLL and base-model forgetting.

Dynamic-writer stage: explicit context reconstruction/continuation, with no source text at the reader and information transmitted through parameter vectors. If the writer sees the full target, this is explicitly defined autoencoding, not a fair pure-causal-LM perplexity comparison with the base model.

Then test QA/paraphrases from new articles and counterfactual A/B writes: real bank versus shuffled values/empty, same-fact paraphrases, and unrelated-question retention. Qualify the teacher format on training entities before sealing.

required_measurements: Hard top1 / top-k coverage: fixed token windows, per-layer/head and cumulative training statistics separately.
Actual read-weight entropy, effective slots exp(H), largest-slot mass, and top1% mass; do not reward uniformity alone.
Per-slot value-gradient norm distribution, fraction above fixed epsilon, update intervals, parameter deltas, and unvisited-window counts.
Query/key/value norms, cosine distributions, residual-injection strength, train/held-out NLL, and base-task retention.
Full EM/F1 on teacher-validated new-article QA, gains over bank controls, strict correctness in both A/B worlds with answers changing appropriately, and unrelated-fact retention.
Separately record support-writing backbone tokens, training-read backbone tokens, dense aggregation/clustering costs, checkpoint size, and sparse CPU-VDB deployment throughput.
decision_rule: Higher usage without improved dev NLL or real new-fact readout does not establish a solution to sparse degeneration. If dense training clearly beats sparse and retains gains under the same sparse evaluation, that supports the optimization-coverage hypothesis. If all strategies fail, investigate low-rank/single-layer reader capacity and writer information bottlenecks.
reporting_limits: Every recommendation is a new hypothesis test. Neither theoretical feasibility nor another method’s full-model, large-scale pretraining results establish implementation or success in this project.
Do not directly attribute the preceding three failures to sample count, sparsity, or templates alone. New experiments need controls that distinguish these factors.
public_record_note: This preserves the original primary-source reading log before implementation. Proposal entries are literature-review suggestions, not claims about the executed experiment. See docs/coldstart_protocol.md for the fixed eight-arm pilot.
